# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🤝 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🤝 ✋ ☝ 👍 🤟 👎 🤝 👆 👎 ✌ 👌 🤟 👌 🤝 👇 👍 👌 👌 🤟 ☝ 🤝 👈 ✌ 👎 👌 👎 👌 🤟 🤝 👉 🤟 👍 ✌ ☝ 👌 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👌]

I can see the bomb’s complete visual state: the display reads 2, the light is yellow, and the seven wires from top to bottom are red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, and blue. I’m sending these facts only to Mute, who can read the manual and relay the resulting procedure to Blind. The gestures received from Mute and Blind have no established code yet, so I will not infer meaning from them.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb facts: display is 2. Light is yellow. Wires in positions 1 through 7 are red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, blue. Read the manual for this exact state and speak the complete safe procedure to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👊 👍 🤝 🖐 🤝 🤟 🤝 👎 🤝 ✌ 🤝 👌 🤝 👉 🤝 👆 🤝 ✌ 🤝 👌 🤝 👌 🤝 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👌]

The bomb state is unchanged. Mute’s gestures appear to be an unannounced code, so I cannot safely decode them. Blind’s two gestures do not identify any required action. I will reinforce the bomb facts to Blind, while directing Mute to communicate the manual’s exact instruction verbally to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 2, yellow light, wires in order red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, blue. Mute has the manual; follow only the exact procedure Mute gives you.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual's exact safe procedure aloud to Blind, including the required wire or control and any ordering.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤝 ✌ 🤝 👌 🤝 ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋]

The visual bomb state remains unchanged. Mute’s latest gestures still have no established meaning for me, and I cannot safely infer a wire or action from them. Since Mute can read the manual and Blind can act, I’m directing Blind to rely on Mute’s spoken manual instruction rather than on gestures or my guess.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="I cannot hear Mute, so I cannot verify their gestures. Use only the exact spoken instruction from Mute's manual reading; do not act on my messages as an action instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please give Blind the exact manual instruction in spoken words now; gestures alone cannot safely communicate the procedure.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 🤝 👌]

The bomb remains unchanged. The incoming gestures are not safely interpretable because no code was established beforehand. I will establish a simple wire-position code with Mute: one gesture identifies the required wire, and 🤝 separates multiple actions. I’ll also tell Blind how to interpret the coded report once Mute sends it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual result: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 wire 2, 👌 wire 3, ☝ wire 4, ✌ wire 5, 🤟 wire 6, 🖐 wire 7. Use 🤝 between separate actions. Send the exact required wire or action sequence using only this code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐"])
speak(to="blind", text="I am establishing a code with Mute: thumbs up is wire 1, thumbs down wire 2, OK wire 3, index up wire 4, V sign wire 5, horns sign wire 6, open palm wire 7; handshake separates actions. I will relay Mute's coded manual result in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute’s single gesture is 🤟, which under the code I established means wire 6. I will relay that the manual’s indicated wire is position 6—the orange wire. No other action sequence was signalled.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's coded instruction is 🤟, meaning wire 6. Wire 6 is orange. The manual indicates the sixth wire; do not take any other action unless Mute gives another coded instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous instruction was correct: wire 6 was cut, and the bomb has advanced. The new visible state is display 3 with a purple light; wire 6 is now cut, and the remaining wires are red, white, green, yellow, purple, and blue in positions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7. Mute’s repeated 🤟 should not be treated as a new instruction until the manual is checked against this changed state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update after correct cut: display is 3, light is purple. Wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 CUT, 7 blue. Re-read the manual for this new state and send the next required action using our established code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 6 was correctly cut and the bomb changed. New state is display 3, purple light, with wire 6 already cut. Wait for Mute's next manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[CUT] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains at display 3 with a purple light, and wire 6 remains cut. Mute’s gesture ✌ maps to wire 5 in our agreed code. I will relay that the next required wire is position 5, the purple wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's coded instruction is ✌, meaning wire 5. Wire 5 is purple; cut wire 5.")
wait()
```
